title: Into the Wild
author: Jon Krakauer
one_line_takeaway: Chris McCandless's journey into the Alaskan wilderness was neither madness nor mere arrogance but an idealistic young man's intense hunger for authenticity, and Krakauer reconstructs it to ask what drives people toward risk and solitude.
synopsis: In April 1992 Christopher McCandless, a recent Emory University graduate from a well-off Virginia family, walked alone into the wilderness north of Mount McKinley; months later his body was found in an abandoned bus along the Stampede Trail. Jon Krakauer, who first wrote about the case for Outside magazine, reconstructs the two years before: McCandless gave his savings to charity, abandoned his car, cut off his family, renamed himself Alexander Supertramp and drifted across the American West — working a South Dakota grain elevator, kayaking down the Colorado River into Mexico, living among rubber tramps at the Slabs, and befriending people such as Wayne Westerberg and the elderly Ronald Franz. Drawing on McCandless's journals, photographs and marked-up books by Thoreau, Tolstoy and Jack London, as well as interviews with those he met, Krakauer explores the family tensions behind his flight and compares him with other idealists who vanished into wild places, such as Everett Ruess and Gene Rosellini. He weaves in his own reckless youthful climb of the Devils Thumb in Alaska to understand McCandless's pull toward risk, and weighs competing explanations for how he died.

parts.title: The Discovery
parts.summary: The book opens with McCandless's final hitchhike into Alaska and the discovery of his body, setting up the question of who he was and why he went.

parts.title: The Drifter Years
parts.summary: Krakauer traces McCandless's two years on the road across the West, the people he met and the new identity he took on, shedding possessions and ties.

parts.title: Family and Motives
parts.summary: Interviews with family and friends reveal the tensions of McCandless's upbringing and the books and ideals that shaped his rejection of conventional life.

parts.title: Kindred Spirits
parts.summary: Krakauer sets McCandless beside other young idealists who disappeared into the wild, and his own dangerous solo climb, to probe what draws people to extreme risk.

parts.title: The Alaska Months
parts.summary: Reconstructing McCandless's time in the Alaskan bush from his journal and photographs, Krakauer examines what went wrong and the competing theories of his death.
